chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The guardianship (walayah) is for the one who emancipates.'

key_terms.الْوَلَاءُ: Guardianship or manumission bond; the legal relationship between a master and the slave he frees.

ai.seo_question: Who has the right of guardianship over a freed slave in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Shaykh al-Kulayni, establishes the principle of 'al-walayah li-man a'taq', signifying that the master who emancipates a slave becomes their legal patron (mawla). This bond creates a permanent social and legal tie, granting the emancipator rights of inheritance and guardianship, a concept deeply rooted in pre-Islamic and early Islamic jurisprudence. It underscores the transition of the freed slave from property to a dependent member of the patron's family unit under Shia legal tradition.
